chapter: Sunset Cafe, Pass in Review and rebuilding the band
title: The Sunset All Stars under Cal Dickerson and Randolph's Peanut Vendor audition
summary: Glaser hired Cal Dickerson to put together the Sunset band; Armstrong had insisted on Randolph, who won Glaser over by playing and singing The Peanut Vendor in Armstrong's manner.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You were talking about the Sunset All Stars. And you said that Jabbo Smith was in there, and Zinky Zooty Singleton. Was Preston Jackson in the band?
Preston Jackson was on trombone, and Eddie Fante was on trombone.
Oh, they had two trombones?
Two trombones. Eddie Fante -- they had Guy Kelly on trumpet.
He had three trumpets and two trombones.
Three trumpets and two trombones. And -- let's see, who was on -- I'm trying to think of the tenor man that they had.
Was it Al Washington?

I don't think we had Al in the band.
Not that band. No, I can't think -- who was on the -- but, anyway, Dickerson was heading the band.
Oh, he'd come back from New York after going there with Louis, and went back to the Sunset. Joe
Glaser --

Joe Glaser had Cal Dickerson. He was going to open the Sunset, so he hired Cal Dickerson to get the band. So Cal Dickerson was picking out the men. Louis told Joe that he was coming to town, you know, he was coming back, and as near as I can remember, now, he had -- he told Cal Dickerson to -- whoever you put on -- I don't care who else you have on trumpet, but you gotta have Randolph.
But I didn't know at the time that Louis had told Joe to have -- to put me in the band. So when Joe Glaser came to hear the band -- this was funny, so he featured everybody in the band but me.
Cal Dickerson did?
Yes, everybody in the band but me.
Now this was after you left Bernie Young. This was about 1930?
This was in 19 -- I believe it was, yes. But this is before Louis came back from --
Yes.

France. And so, Cal Dickerson said, "Well, that's all now. Let's Just go." Then Joe says, "Well, what about that man over there?" Well, see, Cal Dickerson didn't have -- he really didn't want me. He didn't want me in the band, but I was just in there because Joe had an angle. See, Joe was giving me a job, because he's going to have me to
organize the band for Louis. And I didn't know Louis was telling Joe this, you see.
Oh, I see.

I didn't know this was going on. So Al Dickerson says -- he leaned over on the piano, he says, like this, "What are you going to play, man?" And so, I obliged him. I was full of accommodations that day, and I said, "The Peanut Vendor", man."
(Laughter.)
So, I played The Peanut Vendor. So knowing that Joe liked Louis on the trumpet, and sang it like Louis.
Oh, yeah?
And Joe got a kick out of that.
